Chronology 9 — Eschatology: The End

The storyline closes where it began — with the seam intact.

Striking agreement

Both texts affirm: a coming end of the age; bodily resurrection of the dead; a universal Day of Judgment; heaven and hell as real destinations; the return of Jesus; a great deceiver figure; and final, perfect justice.

What each actually says:

  • Bible: the trumpet and the dead raised (1 Thess 4:16; 1 Cor 15:52); the resurrection body (1 Cor 15:42–44); judgment "each according to what he has done" (Matt 25:31–46; Rev 20:12) — note: even the Bible judges by deeds as evidence; new heaven and new earth, "no more death", and "they will see His face" (Rev 21:1–4; 22:4).
  • Qurʾan: the trumpet (ṣūr, Q 39:68); the Quaking and "an atom's weight" weighed (Q 99:7–8); the Balance (mīzān, Q 23:102–103; 101:6–9); the records given in right/left hand (Q 69:19–25); and — correcting a common caricature — a beatific vision: "faces, that Day, radiant, looking at their Lord" (Q 75:22–23). (The Bridge (ṣirāṭ) and many hell/paradise specifics are ḥadīth, flagged as tradition, not Qurʾan.)

Precision (Methodology §1): the Dajjal is principally hadith, not Qur'an; the Antichrist is principally the Johannine epistles and tradition, lightly in the NT. Both "deceiver" motifs are flagged as more traditional than scriptural, on each side equally.

The decisive divergences

1. The criterion of salvation — the seam's terminus

  • Islam: judgment by faith + deeds, under God's sovereign mercy/will; no atonement is needed (direct downstream of cap. 11 and cap. 09 §2.4).
  • Christianity: salvation by grace through Christ's atoning work, received by faith — because the cap. 11 Fall created a debt only the cap. 16 cross pays.

The same fork from the garden determines the gate of paradise. This is the seam's endpoint: one continuous logical thread from creation to judgment.

2. Jesus' role at the end

  • Islam: returns as a Muslim, breaks the cross, defeats the Dajjal, affirms Islam, then dies.
  • Christianity: returns as the divine Judge and King.
  • Same figure, mutually exclusive roles — the cap. 05/16 divergence projected onto the last day.

3. Mediation

  • Islam — limited intercession (shafāʿa) by God's leave; Christianity — Christ the one mediator (1 Tim 2:5). This is the cap. 16 divergence, not a new one.

Slogans that dissolve on inspection

Two popular contrasts are overdrawn and, by the dossier's method (dissolve the slogan, keep the real seam), must be corrected — against both sides:

  • "Islam = works, Christianity = grace." False as stated. The Bible judges by deeds (Matt 25; James 2:24 "justified by works") and teaches grace (Eph 2:8–9); Islam teaches deeds and that "none enters Paradise by his deeds — only by God's mercy" (a sound ḥadīth) and rests on God's raḥma (cap. 09). Both hold faith, works, and grace together. The irreducible difference is not works-vs-grace; it is atonement vs. no-atonement (cap. 11/16).
  • "Qurʾanic paradise = physical, biblical heaven = spiritual." False. The Qurʾan has the beatific vision (Q 75:22–23) and the Bible has a physical new earth, feasting, and no more death (Rev 21). Both are *physical and God-centred; the hūr* verses (Q 44:54; 55:56) are also linguistically debated and are not the caricature.

Arbiter verdict — the end

Present. A large shared eschatological frame; decisive divergence on the mechanism of salvation and Christ's identity/role.

Weigh.

  • Strong shared structure: resurrection, judgment, heaven/hell, returning Christ, deceiver, final justice, and even a beatific vision — substantive, not vague.
  • Slogans dissolved: "works vs. grace" and "physical vs. spiritual paradise" are both false as stated — corrected against both sides.
  • The one irreducible divergence: atonement vs. no-atonement (plus Christ's identity at the end) — the logical terminus of the cap. 11 fork, which cannot be true both ways.
  • Symmetric flags: the deceiver motifs (Dajjāl / Antichrist) and many paradise/hell specifics are traditional more than scriptural on both sides.

Judge. On the eschatological scaffolding: a strong draw — notably similar, even more so once the false contrasts are removed. On the one real divergence (atonement and Christ's identity): not arbitrable — each system is internally coherent, and which is true is a theological-truth question the arbiter has, from the start, declined (Methodology §5). The honest yield of the whole chronology is that most "knockout" contrasts shrink on inspection to one genuine, non-decidable seam.

The whole arc — one seam, restated

StageThe single dividing question
God's natureSimple/transcendent, or triune/incarnational love?
CreationDoes God "rest" / enter creaturely terms?
The FallIs sin inherited (→ redeemer needed)?
Flood / AbrahamSalvation by lineage, or by personal faith?
Moses / DavidAre prophets fallible, or impeccable?
JesusDid the cross happen, and what is Jesus?
MuhammadIs revelation sealed, and is he foretold?
The EndSaved by atonement, or by deeds under mercy?

Final word of Part III. The deepened reading sharpens, not softens, the result. Most of the famous "knockout" contrasts — guilt-transfer, sinful-vs-sinless prophets, works-vs-grace, physical-vs-spiritual heaven, even "did Jesus die" — shrink on close inspection, because each scripture's own text is more internally mixed than the slogans admit (Ezek 18 inside the Bible; repenting prophets inside the Qurʾan; grace inside Islam; deeds inside the Gospel). What remains after the slogans dissolve is one continuous, traceable seam: inherited need → atonement → the identity and death of Christ → the gate of salvation. On the bare historical questions (the crucifixion as event; manuscript-based prophecy claims) the neutral method does lean, by the same rule applied to both sides. On that one theological seam, the arbiter's consistent verdict is the honest one: internally coherent on each side, and not decidable by evidence or logic alone — which is exactly what neutrality, held to the end, looks like.
